# Core metrics reference

This reference is generated from the Weaver semantic convention registry in
[`semconv/groups/metric.engine.yaml`][metric-engine] and
[`semconv/groups/attributes.metrics.yaml`][attrs-metrics]. Regenerate it after
schema changes with:

```bash
cd rust/otap-dataflow
cargo xtask telemetry-codegen --update
```

For OTLP and Prometheus mapping rules, entity attribute sets, and runtime
telemetry policy levels, see [Self-observability](../self-observability.md).

| `pipeline.completion.nack.attempted` | `pipeline.completion` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of Nack completions routed toward an interested upstream node. This is the failure-side counterpart to attempted Acks and captures how many downstream refusals found an upstream subscriber and entered the delivery path. Level: `normal`. |
| `pipeline.completion.nack.delivered` | `pipeline.completion` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of Nack control messages actually delivered to upstream nodes. This is the delivery-side counterpart to attempted Nacks and helps distinguish routing intent from successful node-control delivery under backpressure. Level: `normal`. |
| `pipeline.completion.nack.dropped_no_interest` | `pipeline.completion` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of Nack completions dropped because no upstream frame was interested. This is particularly important for liveness and correctness analysis: it means failure information reached the dispatcher but no upstream frame subscribed to receive it. Level: `normal`. |
| `pipeline.completion.pending_sends.buffered` | `pipeline.completion` | `gauge` | `Gauge<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Number of completion deliveries currently buffered for later retry. A sustained backlog here means the completion dispatcher is making progress by deferring sends to full node-control inboxes instead of blocking, but it also indicates unwind traffic is under pressure. Level: `basic`. |
| `pipeline.completion.unwind.depth` | `pipeline.completion` | `histogram` | `Mmsc` | `{frame}` | none | `development` | Distribution of unwind stack depth consumed per completion outcome. Larger values indicate completions are traversing more frames before finding an interested upstream node or concluding that none exists, which helps explain completion-path cost and routing behavior. Level: `detailed`. |
| `pipeline.context.switches.involuntary` | `pipeline` | `counter` | `ObserveCounter<u64>` | `{1}` | none | `development` | Number of times the pipeline thread was preempted by the scheduler since start. A rising rate often indicates CPU contention or time-slice expirations. When paired with `cpu_utilization`, it helps diagnose CPU time lost to preemption. |
| `pipeline.context.switches.voluntary` | `pipeline` | `counter` | `ObserveCounter<u64>` | `{1}` | none | `development` | Number of times the pipeline thread voluntarily yielded the CPU since start. A rising rate can indicate scheduling pressure due to blocking work (I/O, locks, backpressure) and helps distinguish "waiting" from "CPU-bound". |

| `pipeline.cpu.utilization` | `pipeline` | `gauge` | `Gauge<f64>` | `{1}` | none | `development` | Difference in pipeline cpu time since the last measurement, divided by the elapsed time. Reported as a ratio in the range `[0, 1]`. |

| `pipeline.memory.allocated.delta` | `pipeline` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{By}` | none | `development` | Bytes allocated to the heap by this pipeline during the last measurement window. |
| `pipeline.memory.freed` | `pipeline` | `counter` | `ObserveCounter<u64>` | `{By}` | none | `development` | Memory freed to the heap by the pipeline instance since start. |

| `pipeline.memory.usage` | `pipeline` | `updowncounter` | `ObserveUpDownCounter<u64>` | `{By}` | none | `development` | The amount of heap memory in use by the pipeline instance running on a specific core. |
| `pipeline.page.faults.major` | `pipeline` | `counter` | `ObserveCounter<u64>` | `{1}` | none | `development` | Number of major page faults (requiring disk I/O) since start. Any non-trivial rate typically indicates severe memory pressure or swapping, and correlates strongly with pipeline latency spikes. |
| `pipeline.page.faults.minor` | `pipeline` | `counter` | `ObserveCounter<u64>` | `{1}` | none | `development` | Number of minor page faults (served without disk I/O) since start. A rising rate indicates memory access pain (poor locality, working-set churn), even if heap bytes are stable. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.cancel_telemetry_timer.received` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of telemetry timer cancel requests received by the runtime manager. | `pipeline.runtime_control.cancel_timer.received` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of `CancelTimer` control messages received by the runtime manager. | `pipeline.runtime_control.collect_telemetry.sent` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of `CollectTelemetry` control messages sent to nodes. This helps confirm telemetry timers are progressing under load and that observability work is not being starved by other runtime-control traffic. Level: `normal`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.downstream_shutdown.sent` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of downstream `Shutdown` fan-out operations to non-receivers. This marks the handoff from receiver draining to downstream convergence, which is useful when debugging where shutdown latency is spent. Level: `normal`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.drain.active` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `gauge` | `Gauge<u64>` | `{1}` | none | `development` | Whether the runtime is currently in graceful drain mode. This is the top-level liveness phase signal for shutdown analysis: `1` means ingress has been stopped and the runtime is trying to converge to quiescence, `0` means normal operation. Level: `basic`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.drain.pending_receivers` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `gauge` | `Gauge<u64>` | `{node}` | none | `development` | Number of receivers that still need to report `ReceiverDrained`. This shows whether shutdown is still blocked in the receiver-first drain phase and helps identify a stuck or slow receiver delaying downstream shutdown. Level: `basic`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.drain.receiver_phase_duration_ns` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `histogram` | `Mmsc` | `ns` | none | `development` | Distribution of time spent waiting for receivers to finish draining. This isolates the receiver-gated phase of shutdown and is useful for determining whether slow graceful shutdown is ingress-bound or further downstream in the pipeline. Level: `detailed`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.drain.total_duration_ns` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `histogram` | `Mmsc` | `ns` | none | `development` | Distribution of total graceful shutdown duration for the runtime. This is the top-level latency metric for shutdown liveness and shows how long the runtime took to move from shutdown acceptance to completion or forced deadline exit. Level: `detailed`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.drain_ingress.sent` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of `DrainIngress` fan-out operations sent to receivers. This confirms that shutdown moved from "requested" to "stop admitting new ingress", which is the first active liveness step of graceful drain. Level: `normal`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.pending_sends.buffered` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `gauge` | `Gauge<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Number of node-control deliveries currently buffered for later retry. A sustained non-zero value indicates the runtime manager is no longer delivering control work immediately and is absorbing backpressure from full node-control inboxes instead of blocking the runtime. Level: `basic`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.receiver_drained.received` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of `ReceiverDrained` notifications received from receivers. | `pipeline.runtime_control.shutdown.deadline_forced` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of shutdowns that reached the deadline before natural completion. | `pipeline.runtime_control.shutdown.received` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of `RuntimeControlMsg::Shutdown` requests accepted by this runtime. | `pipeline.runtime_control.start_telemetry_timer.received` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of telemetry timer start requests received by the runtime manager. | `pipeline.runtime_control.start_timer.received` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of `StartTimer` control messages received by the runtime manager. This helps quantify timer creation pressure and can explain growth in `timers.active` or bursts of later `timer_tick.sent` activity. Level: `normal`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.telemetry_timers.active` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `gauge` | `Gauge<u64>` | `{timer}` | none | `development` | Number of telemetry collection timers currently registered. This distinguishes telemetry scheduling pressure from normal timer traffic and helps explain unexpected `CollectTelemetry` activity. Level: `basic`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.timer_tick.sent` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Count of `TimerTick` control messages sent to nodes. This confirms that due timers are actually being delivered and helps detect starvation where timers accumulate but ticks do not make progress. Level: `normal`. |
| `pipeline.runtime_control.timers.active` | `pipeline.runtime_control` | `gauge` | `Gauge<u64>` | `{timer}` | none | `development` | Number of ordinary per-node timers currently registered. This is useful for understanding timer pressure and for spotting leaks where timers are started but not canceled or consumed as expected. Level: `basic`. |
| `pipeline.uptime` | `pipeline` | `gauge` | `Gauge<f64>` | `{s}` | none | `development` | The time the pipeline instance has been running. |
| `tokio.runtime.blocking.task.queue.size` | `tokio.runtime` | `updowncounter` | `ObserveUpDownCounter<u64>` | `{task}` | none | `development` | Current number of tasks pending in the blocking thread pool. This counts tasks spawned using `spawn_blocking` that have not yet started. |
| `tokio.runtime.blocking.thread.count` | `tokio.runtime` | `updowncounter` | `ObserveUpDownCounter<u64>` | `{thread}` | none | `development` | Current number of threads created for the blocking thread pool. |
| `tokio.runtime.blocking.thread.idle.count` | `tokio.runtime` | `updowncounter` | `ObserveUpDownCounter<u64>` | `{thread}` | none | `development` | Current number of idle threads in the blocking thread pool. |
| `tokio.runtime.budget.forced.yield.count` | `tokio.runtime` | `counter` | `ObserveCounter<u64>` | `{yield}` | none | `development` | Total number of times tasks were forced to yield after exhausting their cooperative budget. This metric requires `tokio_unstable` and 64-bit atomics. |
| `tokio.runtime.global.task.queue.size` | `tokio.runtime` | `updowncounter` | `ObserveUpDownCounter<u64>` | `{task}` | none | `development` | Current number of tasks pending in the runtime's global/injection queue. This queue is used when tasks are spawned or woken from outside the runtime. |
| `tokio.runtime.io.driver.fd.deregistered.count` | `tokio.runtime` | `counter` | `ObserveCounter<u64>` | `{fd}` | none | `development` | Total number of file descriptors deregistered from the runtime's I/O driver. | `tokio.runtime.io.driver.fd.registered.count` | `tokio.runtime` | `counter` | `ObserveCounter<u64>` | `{fd}` | none | `development` | Total number of file descriptors registered with the runtime's I/O driver. This metric requires `tokio_unstable` and 64-bit atomics (and Tokio's `net` feature). |
| `tokio.runtime.io.driver.ready.count` | `tokio.runtime` | `counter` | `ObserveCounter<u64>` | `{ready}` | none | `development` | Total number of ready events processed by the runtime's I/O driver. This metric requires `tokio_unstable` and 64-bit atomics (and Tokio's `net` feature). |

## Channels, nodes, and flows

On `channel.sender` and `channel.receiver`, the `channel.kind` entity attribute
distinguishes `pdata` channels (which carry the `signal` datapoint attribute)
from `control` channels.

| OTLP metric name | Scope (`otel_scope_name`) | Instrument | Rust type(s) | Unit | Datapoint attributes | Stability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `channel.receiver.capacity` | `channel.receiver` | `gauge` | `Gauge<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Configured maximum number of buffered messages. |
| `channel.receiver.messages` | `channel.receiver` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | `signal` | `development` | Messages successfully dequeued from the channel. |
| `channel.receiver.queue.depth` | `channel.receiver` | `gauge` | `Gauge<u64>` | `{message}` | none | `development` | Current number of messages buffered in the channel. |
| `channel.sender.failures` | `channel.sender` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | `error.type`, `signal` | `development` | Failed or refused immediate send attempts. |
| `channel.sender.messages` | `channel.sender` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | `outcome`, `signal` | `development` | Messages whose immediate channel send attempt terminated. |
| `flow.compute.duration` | `flow.compute` | `histogram` | `Mmsc` / `HistogramNormal` / `HistogramDetailed` | `s` | `signal` | `development` | Sum of per-node compute durations, in seconds, for messages traversing the flow range. |

## Shared receiver and exporter boundaries

| OTLP metric name | Scope (`otel_scope_name`) | Instrument | Rust type(s) | Unit | Datapoint attributes | Stability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exporter.attempted.duration` | `exporter.attempted` | `histogram` | `Mmsc` / `HistogramNormal` / `HistogramDetailed` | `s` | `outcome`, `signal` | `development` | Time spent performing export attempts, including backend latency. |
| `exporter.attempted.items` | `exporter.attempted` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{item}` | `outcome`, `signal` | `development` | Number of signal items handled across export attempts. |
| `exporter.attempted.messages` | `exporter.attempted` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | `outcome`, `signal` | `development` | Number of node-local delivery attempts. Retries represented as shared attempts count again. This differs from `node.input.messages`, which counts PData messages entering the exporter. |
| `exporter.attempted.payload.size` | `exporter.attempted` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `By` | `outcome`, `signal` | `development` | Encoded application payload size produced or submitted across export attempts. |
| `exporter.exports.duration` | `exporter.exports` | `histogram` | `HistogramNormal` | `s` | `outcome`, `signal` | `development` | Time from dequeuing PData through its terminal local or backend export result. Ack/Nack notification time is excluded. |
| `exporter.exports.messages` | `exporter.exports` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | `outcome`, `signal` | `development` | Number of messages whose export reached a terminal outcome. |
| `receiver.messages.bytes` | `receiver.messages` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `By` | `signal` | `development` | Encoded transport payload bytes admitted to the pipeline send path. |
| `receiver.messages.completed` | `receiver.messages` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | `signal` | `development` | Number of admitted messages whose receiver work terminated. |
| `receiver.messages.started` | `receiver.messages` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | `signal` | `development` | Number of decoded messages admitted to the pipeline send path. |
| `receiver.processing.duration` | `receiver.processing` | `histogram` | `Mmsc` / `HistogramNormal` / `HistogramDetailed` | `s` | none | `development` | Node-defined receiver-local processing time. Each receiver documents its stable start and end boundary. Downstream processing, batching wait, handoff wait, and Ack/Nack completion are excluded. |
| `receiver.pulled.attempts` | `receiver.pulled` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{attempt}` | `outcome` | `development` | Number of accepted collection attempts reaching a terminal local outcome. |
| `receiver.received.messages` | `receiver.received` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `{message}` | `outcome`, `signal` | `development` | Number of classified external messages whose receiver-local handling terminated. |
| `receiver.received.payload.size` | `receiver.received` | `counter` | `Counter<u64>` | `By` | `outcome`, `signal` | `development` | Encoded application payload size observed before receiver decoding. |

## Datapoint and registration attributes

| Attribute | Wire type | Examples | Stability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bucket.range.us` | `string` | `[0,100)`, `[100,200)`, `[900,+inf)` | `development` | Microsecond poll-time histogram bucket range (lower inclusive, upper exclusive). |
| `console.stream` | `string` | `stdout`, `stderr` | `development` | Standard output stream served by the console output writer. |
| `dimension` | `string` | `bytes`, `messages` | `development` | Weight dimension metered by the rate admission limiter. |
| `error.type` | `string` | `timeout`, `java.net.UnknownHostException`, `server_certificate_invalid`, `500` | `stable` | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. |
| `outcome` | `string` | `success`, `failure`, `refused` | `development` | Terminal outcome of the recorded pipeline or component operation. |
| `refusal` | `string` | `would_throttle`, `throttle`, `oversized` | `development` | Reason a rate admission point declined, or would have declined, a request. |
| `signal` | `string` | `traces`, `metrics`, `logs` | `development` | OpenTelemetry pipeline signal associated with the metric recording. |
